description: Introduce exactly ONE shared High/Fast quality concept for the whole site and improve the lighting/visual quality of ALL FOUR 3D scenes consistently, adapting the tireshop techniques. This is the core WS2 feature. Depends on FEAT-001 (baseline + frame-time harness). frankfabric has NO quality selector today, so ADD exactly one shared quality concept (a single small module + one control surface) and thread it through all four scenes - do NOT invent a different ad-hoc system per scene. Per scene: build a proper key/fill/bounce light rig, soften shadow edges, ensure ContactShadows anchors the subject (already present in all four - tune, don't duplicate), and add depth to the ground/backdrop materials (and floor/wall where a scene has them). Gate the HEAVIER effects (soft/contact shadows, higher shadow-map resolution, extra lights, environment) behind the High path; the Fast path must stay AT LEAST as cheap as today. Respect each scene's tone-mapping decision under CONSTRAINT #2 (measurement-gated).
steps: Design the single shared quality concept. Create a lightweight, zero-three module (e.g. components/three/quality.ts) exporting a `Quality = 'high' | 'fast'` type, a default, and a tiny React context/hook (e.g. QualityProvider + useQuality) OR a small shared hook that reads/writes a quality preference. Keep it ZERO three.js imports so it does not drag the heavy three chunk into any static page bundle (mirror how components/wardrobe/wardrobeOptions.ts stays three-free to preserve WS1's chunk-split win). Model the semantics on tireshop's selector (src/ui/Panels.jsx: 'High - shadows on' / 'Fast - shadows off') and on ShopStage.jsx's use of quality: High => shadows enabled, dpr [1,2], higher shadow-map res, soft/contact shadows, extra lights/environment; Fast => shadows off or minimal, lower dpr cap, no soft shadows, minimal lights. This is the ONE system; all four scenes consume it.

Add ONE small, consistent quality control surface so a user can switch High/Fast, wired to the shared module. Prefer a single reusable control component (e.g. components/three/QualityToggle.tsx) rendered near each scene's canvas within its existing chatbot/builder/pet wrapper (CoachChatbot.tsx, ChefChatbot.tsx, WardrobeBuilder.tsx, VirtualPet.tsx). Keep it visually minimal and consistent; do NOT disturb the recently-fixed chat/UI layout - place it unobtrusively (e.g. a small labelled select/toggle in an existing controls area). It must be the SAME control/concept everywhere, not four different ad-hoc widgets.

Thread quality into each Canvas. Each of the four scenes accepts a `quality` prop (from the shared hook/context) and applies it: gate `shadows` on the Canvas by quality (tireshop pattern: shadows only on High); set dpr by quality (High [1,2], Fast a cheaper cap like [0.75,1.25] or [1,1.5] - Fast must be NO MORE expensive than today's [1,2] default; note that lowering the Fast dpr is an allowed way to keep Fast at-least-as-cheap while High matches today). Do this WITHOUT touching camera framing constants (position/fov/AIM_HEIGHT/CAMERA_DISTANCE) or any pose/motion transform constants.

Coach scene (components/coach/CoachScene.tsx): replace the ad-hoc ambient+2 directional+hemisphere with a proper key/fill/bounce rig (a shaping key directionalLight, a softer fill from the opposite side, a subtle bounce/rim), near-neutral so the coach OBJ textures keep true color; on High raise the key's shadow-map resolution above today's 1024 and add soft shadow edges (drei <SoftShadows> or ContactShadows blur tuning); on Fast keep it cheap (shadows off, single directional + ambient). Add depth to the GROUND/backdrop - the coach scene currently has only ContactShadows and no floor; consider a subtle ground plane/backdrop material (procedural, no new texture asset if avoidable) that reads with depth, gated to High if it costs. Keep ContactShadows (tune blur/opacity for softer edges); do not float the figure. Respect coach tone mapping (currently ACESFilmic) per CONSTRAINT #2.

Wardrobe scene (components/wardrobe/WardrobeScene.tsx): this is the primary SKIN-BEARING VRM avatar. Build a proper key/fill/bounce rig; on High add soft shadows + higher shadow-map res + optionally a subtle drei <Environment> (prefer a cheap built-in preset or procedural Lightformer over a downloaded HDRI to protect the WS1 byte budget - if any asset would be added, STOP and flag it per CONSTRAINT #6). Add depth to the background/ground (it currently sets a flat #efede8 background + ContactShadows; add a subtle floor/backdrop with material depth). Keep the OrbitControls turntable and ContactShadows. MEASURE skin: if the stronger High lighting makes ACESFilmicToneMapping clip the avatar's skin/face to white, switching THIS scene to THREE.NeutralToneMapping@1.0 is the tireshop-proven fix and is acceptable - but ONLY with a per-scene before/after screenshot proving it fixes the blow-out (CONSTRAINT #2). Do NOT touch the lib/vrm tint pipeline/colors (CONSTRAINT #3).

Chef scene (components/chef/ChefScene.tsx): NOTE it is a Swedish Chef FBX with a matte MeshStandardMaterial (not MToon/VRM) - it still bears a skin/face texture, so the no-blow-out check applies. Build a proper key/fill/bounce rig near-neutral; High adds soft shadows + higher shadow-map res; Fast stays cheap. Add ground/backdrop depth. Keep ContactShadows. Respect tone mapping under CONSTRAINT #2 (measure before changing ACESFilmic).

Pet scene (components/pet/PetScene.tsx): it already has near-neutral warm lighting + ContactShadows. Upgrade to a proper key/fill/bounce rig consistently with the others, soften shadow edges, add ground/backdrop depth (the dog currently floats over only ContactShadows - a subtle ground plane helps it sit). High adds soft shadows + higher shadow-map res; Fast stays cheap. Respect tone mapping under CONSTRAINT #2. Do NOT touch the pet motion transforms just merged in WS1.

Preserve WS1 wins throughout: do NOT add eager preloading; keep OPTIONS in components/wardrobe/wardrobeOptions.ts (three-free); keep the SceneLoader/useProgress Suspense fallback in every scene; keep all four ssr:false dynamic wrappers; route any new asset through lib/asset.ts. If you find you need a new npm dependency, STOP and report the exact package + why instead of installing it (drei ^10 already ships ContactShadows/SoftShadows/AccumulativeShadows/Environment/Lightformer/BakeShadows - use those).

Verify continuously: after wiring, run `npm run lint` (only the expected font warning) and `npm run build` (static export succeeds, all five pages prerender). Confirm no TypeScript/ESLint errors from the new quality module/control and the per-scene changes.

Commit on branch visual/lighting-quality with a conventional-commit message (e.g. `feat(visual): shared High/Fast quality + key/fill/bounce rigs across all four scenes`). Do NOT commit out/, node_modules/, .next/, assets-src/. Record in the feature findings: the exact tone-mapping decision per scene (unchanged vs switched-to-Neutral-with-evidence), any dependency you had to flag, and any asset added with its size.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly ONE shared quality concept exists (a single zero-three module + one reusable control), consumed by all four scenes - NOT four ad-hoc per-scene systems. Grep confirms all four scenes import the same quality source.
Each of the four scenes has a proper key/fill/bounce light rig, retains/tunes ContactShadows so the subject does not float, and has added ground/backdrop material depth.

The High path enables the heavier effects (shadows on, higher shadow-map res than today's 1024, soft/contact shadows, dpr [1,2], any environment); the Fast path is NO MORE expensive than today (shadows off/minimal, dpr cap <= today).

No camera-framing or pose/motion transform constants changed (AIM_HEIGHT, AIM_MODEL_FRACTION, CAMERA_DISTANCE, MODEL_SCALE/TARGET_HEIGHT, gesture/pet motion transforms untouched). lib/vrm tint pipeline/colors untouched.

Any scene whose tone-mapping operator/exposure changed is justified by a per-scene before/after screenshot proving it fixes skin blow-out; scenes left on ACESFilmic are unchanged. No new npm dependency was installed without stopping to flag it.
`npm run lint` clean except the expected font warning; `npm run build` static export succeeds; all five pages prerender.

WS1 wins preserved: OPTIONS still three-free, no eager preload reintroduced, SceneLoader/useProgress fallback intact in all four scenes, all four ssr:false wrappers intact, any new asset routed through asset().
verification: Run `npm run lint` and confirm only the expected font warning.
Run `npm run build` and confirm the static export succeeds and all five route index.html files are emitted in out/.
Grep the four scene files for the shared quality import to confirm a single shared concept is used across all of them (not per-scene ad-hoc).

Grep the four scene files to confirm camera/pose/motion constants (AIM_HEIGHT, CAMERA_DISTANCE, MODEL_SCALE, gesture transforms) are unchanged vs main (git diff main -- <scene> shows lighting/material/quality changes only, no constant edits).
Confirm `git status --short` stages no out/, node_modules/, .next/, or assets-src/ paths.
findings:
IMPLEMENTED. Exactly ONE shared quality concept: new zero-three module components/three/quality.ts (Quality='high'|'fast', DEFAULT_QUALITY='high', qualitySettings() pure mapping, QUALITY_LABELS, and a React QualityProvider/useQuality context) + ONE reusable control components/three/QualityToggle.tsx (segmented High/Fast radiogroup). Both import NO three.js/@react-three/@pixiv (verified by grep) so they do NOT drag the heavy three chunk into any static page bundle - mirrors wardrobeOptions.ts. All FOUR scenes import the same source (grep-confirmed): CoachScene, ChefScene, WardrobeScene, PetScene each take a `quality` prop and derive shadows/dpr/shadowMapSize from qualitySettings(). Each wrapper (CoachChatbot/ChefChatbot/WardrobeBuilder/VirtualPet) now wraps its body in <QualityProvider>, reads useQuality(), renders the SAME <QualityToggle> unobtrusively at the stage's top-left (clear of the top-right mute toggle and bottom label), and threads quality into its Canvas.

HIGH vs FAST: High => Canvas shadows on, dpr [1,2], shadow-map 2048 (above today's 1024), tuned/softer ContactShadows blur, extra rim/back-bounce pointLight, and a subtle procedural ground/backdrop disc for depth. Fast => shadows OFF, dpr [0.75,1.25] (LOWER than today's [1,2], so Fast is strictly at-least-as-cheap), no ground disc, no rim light, minimal rig. High matches today's cost; Fast is cheaper than today.

PER-SCENE LIGHTING: replaced ad-hoc ambient+2directional+hemisphere with a proper near-neutral key(only shadow caster)/fill/bounce(+High rim) rig in all four; added a procedural in-memory CanvasTexture ground disc (radial vignette fading to transparent, no external asset -> zero cold-load byte delta) gated to High for coach/chef/pet (which floated over only ContactShadows) and wardrobe (flat bg got floor depth). Kept + tuned (not duplicated) the EXISTING ContactShadows in every scene (softened blur on High).

TONE MAPPING (CONSTRAINT #2): UNCHANGED in ALL FOUR scenes - all stay THREE.ACESFilmicToneMapping. No operator/exposure changed, so no before/after tone-map screenshot was required. The High rigs were deliberately kept near-neutral with the key intensity held at today's values (wardrobe key stayed 1.4), and spot-check screenshots of the two skin-bearing avatars (wardrobe VRM + chef FBX) under High confirmed NO skin/face blow-out to white (natural skin tone preserved), so switching to NeutralToneMapping was NOT needed. Spot-check screenshots were captured then removed (exhaustive before/after evidence is FEAT-003's job).

SOFTSHADOWS DEVIATION (no dependency/asset flag needed): initially used drei <SoftShadows> on High, but the measure-load harness surfaced a fatal fragment-shader compile error on the wardrobe VRM ('vogelDiskSample function already has a body', Material Name 'Face' ShaderMaterial) - drei SoftShadows rewrites the global shadow-map shader chunk and collides with the VRM's MToon Face ShaderMaterial. Removed <SoftShadows> from ALL four scenes (kept consistent) and softened shadow edges the plan's explicitly-allowed alternative way instead: higher shadow-map resolution (2048) on High + tuned ContactShadows blur. After removal the harness errors dropped back to the 2 expected baseline entries (harness /frankfabric/ root abort + one 404) matching before-*.json.

NO NEW DEPENDENCY, NO NEW ASSET added (only drei's already-shipped ContactShadows used; ground discs are procedural in-memory textures). CHEF-IS-VRM DISCREPANCY confirmed: chef is a Swedish Chef FBX with a matte MeshStandardMaterial (not MToon/VRM); it still bears a skin texture so the no-blow-out check was applied and passed.

WS1 WINS PRESERVED: OPTIONS stays in three-free wardrobeOptions.ts; no eager preload reintroduced; <Suspense fallback={<SceneLoader/>}> useProgress fallback intact in every scene; all four ssr:false dynamic wrappers intact; largest static chunk referenced by the wardrobe page HTML is ~203KB (no ~900KB three chunk eagerly pulled). No camera-framing or pose/motion constants changed (git diff main confirms no AIM_HEIGHT/AIM_MODEL_FRACTION/CAMERA_DISTANCE/MODEL_SCALE/MODEL_TARGET edits); lib/vrm tint pipeline untouched.

VERIFICATION: `npm run lint` clean except the expected @next/next/no-page-custom-font warning (0 errors); `npm run build` static export succeeds with all 5 pages prerendered (out/index.html + 4 project index.html emitted). Node v22.23.2, headless Chrome (SwiftShader software GL) for spot-checks.
